title: Cylindrical object
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. Draw the first two-dimensional sketch by creating a new face and within this face, draw a single loop. In this loop, draw a circle centered at coordinates [0.0544, 0.0544] with a radius of 0.0544. Apply a scale factor of 0.1089 to the two-dimensional sketch to adjust its size. Transform the two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using the Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] and translating it using the translation vector [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Extrude the two-dimensional sketch along the normal direction by 0.75 units to generate the three-dimensional model. Ensure that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction. Perform a boolean operation to create a new solid body using the extruded two-dimensional sketch. The final cylindrical object will have a length of 0.10887096774193548 units, a width of 0.10887096774193548 units, and a height of 0.75 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a circle in the sketch
r = r.center(0.0544, 0.0544).circle(0.0544)

# Extrude the circle to create a cylinder
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the base of the cylinder
sketch = (
    workplane
    .center(0.0544, 0.0544)  # Move to the center of the circle
    .circle(0.0544)  # Draw the circle with the specified radius
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = (
    sketch
    .extrude(0.75)  # Extrude the circle to create the cylinder
)

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = cylinder
